title: The Hidden Cost of Calling Workers Back to the Office

paragraphs.english: This page is an independently written reading guide to a business news report published by The Guardian on 15 July 2025. The reporter is Joanna Partridge, and the paper ran the story as an exclusive. The original article is linked at the foot of this page; what follows is a guide to its numbers and its framing, written for readers who want to follow the English closely.
paragraphs.chinese: 本页是为《卫报》2025 年 7 月 15 日发表的一篇商业新闻报道独立撰写的阅读导读。报道者为 Joanna Partridge，该报以独家报道形式刊出。原文链接见本页页尾；以下是就其数字与叙述框架所写的导读，面向希望细读英文本身的读者。

paragraphs.english: The news itself is a survey. A recruitment company, Hays, questioned 3,600 employers and employees across Britain between late April and early May 2025, and the headline finding is a figure about mood rather than money: 38 per cent of the workers polled said that recent stories about companies tightening their attendance rules had damaged their wellbeing.
paragraphs.chinese: 新闻的内核是一份调查。招聘公司 Hays 在 2025 年 4 月下旬至 5 月上旬访问了英国 3,600 名雇主与雇员，最受关注的结果是一个关于情绪而非金钱的数字：38% 的受访雇员表示，近期那些公司收紧到岗规定的报道已经损害了他们的身心健康。

paragraphs.english: That number is interesting precisely because nothing had yet happened to most of the people reporting it. They were not describing an order they had received; they were describing the effect of expecting one. The report uses the word "fear" in its headline, and the body of the story justifies it, because what such a survey captures is anticipation — the particular strain of waiting to learn whether the shape of your week is about to be rearranged.
paragraphs.chinese: 这个数字之所以有意思，恰恰因为对大多数作出回答的人来说，事情还没有发生。他们描述的不是已经收到的命令，而是预期会有命令所带来的影响。报道在标题里用了“fear（恐惧）”这个词，正文也撑得住它，因为这类调查捕捉的是一种预期——等着知道自己这一周的形状是否即将被重新安排的特别压力。

paragraphs.english: To see why the anticipation is live, the article sets out what firms have been doing. In May, HSBC told staff in its UK high street branches that bonuses might be reduced for those who spent less than 60 per cent of their time at a desk. Barclays and Santander have also been tightening their rules. At the start of June, Man Group, the listed hedge fund, asked its London analysts to come in five days a week for a period while it tried to recover from a run of poor results.
paragraphs.chinese: 要理解这种预期何以真实存在，文章列出了企业近期在做什么。5 月，汇丰告知其英国高街银行网点的员工，若在办公室待的时间不足六成，奖金可能被削减。巴克莱与桑坦德也在收紧规定。6 月初，上市对冲基金 Man Group 要求其伦敦分析师在一段时间内每周到办公室五天，以摆脱一段业绩不佳的时期。

paragraphs.english: Against those moves sits the arrangement most British office workers now have. According to the Office for National Statistics, 28 per cent of working adults in Great Britain were hybrid in the first three months of 2025, splitting the week between home and workplace. The poll puts a satisfaction figure on that group: 84 per cent of hybrid workers said the pattern had a positive effect on their wellbeing, understood to cover mental, physical, social and financial health.
paragraphs.chinese: 与这些举措相对的，是多数英国办公室职员目前的安排。英国国家统计局的数据显示，2025 年第一季度，英国有 28% 的在职成年人采用混合办公，把一周分给家和办公室。调查为这个群体给出了一个满意度数字：84% 的混合办公者表示，这种模式对他们的整体身心状态有正面作用，涵盖心理、身体、社交与财务健康。

paragraphs.english: The gender split inside that figure is modest but consistent. 87 per cent of the women who work hybrid said it had improved their wellbeing, against 80 per cent of the men. When the question turned to the news about mandates, the gap widened: 42 per cent of women said those stories had harmed their wellbeing, against 32 per cent of men. Age divided the sample as well, with workers in their twenties more concerned than colleagues over fifty.
paragraphs.chinese: 这个数字里的性别差异不大但方向一致：采用混合办公的女性中 87% 表示身心状态因此改善，男性为 80%。当问题转向有关强制返岗的新闻时，差距拉开：42% 的女性表示那些报道损害了自己的身心状态，男性为 32%。年龄也把样本分开了，二十多岁的职员比五十岁以上的同事更担心。

paragraphs.english: Money runs underneath nearly all of it. Asked what would make them reluctant to spend more days in the office, 59 per cent pointed to their finances, and the obvious reason is the commute: fares, coffee, lunch, the small daily expenditures that a week at home quietly removes. A wellbeing survey that ignored cost would be measuring the wrong thing, and this one does not ignore it.
paragraphs.chinese: 钱几乎垫在这一切下面。被问到什么会让自己不愿多去办公室时，59% 的人指向自己的财务状况，而显而易见的原因是通勤：车费、咖啡、午饭，那些在家工作的一周里悄悄消失的小额日常开销。一份忽略成本的“身心健康”调查会量错东西，而这一份没有忽略。

paragraphs.english: The article gives the closing word on that point to Hannah Pearsall, Hays's head of wellbeing. Her warning, paraphrased rather than quoted here, is that employers underestimate what a return-to-office push does to staff, financial wellbeing included, and that the consequences could be serious for the business itself. The word she reaches for is "catastrophic", and it is worth noticing that the word is hers, not the reporter's.
paragraphs.chinese: 文章把这一点的收尾发言权交给了 Hays 的身心健康负责人 Hannah Pearsall。她的警告（此处为转述而非引用）是：雇主低估了推动返岗对员工的影响，其中包括财务层面的身心状态，而后果对企业本身也可能很严重。她用的词是“catastrophic（灾难性的）”，值得留意的是这个词属于她，而不属于记者。

paragraphs.english: Read as reporting, the story is careful about where each fact comes from: the percentages belong to Hays, the hybrid share belongs to the ONS, and the corporate examples belong to earlier coverage. What the article does not do is test any of it. No company is shown losing staff, no productivity figure moves in either direction, and no researcher appears to dispute the poll. A reader who wants the other side of the argument has to supply it.
paragraphs.chinese: 作为报道来读，这篇稿子在每个事实的来源上都很谨慎：百分比属于 Hays，混合办公比例属于国家统计局，企业案例属于此前的报道。文章没有做的是检验其中任何一项。没有哪家公司被呈现为正在流失员工，生产率数字没有朝任何方向变动，也没有研究者出面质疑这份调查。想要另一边论点的读者，只能自己补上。

paragraphs.english: That missing side is not hard to reconstruct. Employers who want people back tend to cite collaboration, the training of junior staff, and buildings half empty on a lease they are still paying for. Whether those arguments are good is a separate question; the point here is structural. A survey commissioned by a recruitment firm measures what workers feel, and feelings are exactly what it is built to measure.
paragraphs.chinese: 缺的那一边并不难重建。希望员工回来的雇主通常会说协作、说年轻员工的培养、说还在付租金却半空的楼。这些理由是否成立是另一个问题；这里的要点是结构性的：由招聘公司委托的调查衡量的是员工的感受，而感受正是它被设计来衡量之物。

paragraphs.english: There is a second reason to read the numbers slowly. The 38 per cent and the 84 per cent do not share a base. The first is a share of all the workers surveyed, the second a share of the hybrid workers inside that group, and news writing compresses such distinctions because space is short. The compression is where careless reading begins: a percentage without its base is a rumour with a decimal point.
paragraphs.chinese: 还有第二个理由要求把数字读慢一点。38% 和 84% 并不共享同一个分母。前者是全部受访职员中的比例，后者是该群体中混合办公者的比例，而新闻写作因为篇幅紧张会压缩这类区分。压缩正是粗心阅读开始的地方：一个没有分母的百分比，就是带着小数点的传言。

paragraphs.english: The vocabulary carries assumptions too. A "return-to-office mandate" sounds like a rule handed down, and in most of the cases described it is one. "Hybrid" sounds like a compromise, and for the workers polled it functions as the arrangement they are defending. "Wellbeing" is the softest word in the story and the one doing the most work, since it allows a dispute about money, time and autonomy to be reported as a dispute about health.
paragraphs.chinese: 用词也带着预设。“return-to-office mandate（返岗强制令）”听起来像自上而下的规定，而文中描述的大多数情形确实如此。“Hybrid（混合）”听起来像折中，而对受访职员来说，它其实是被捍卫的现状。“Wellbeing（身心状态）”是全文最软的一个词，也是承担最多工作的词，因为它让一场关于金钱、时间与自主权的争执，被报道成一场关于健康的争执。

paragraphs.english: What the piece establishes, then, is narrow and useful: in the summer of 2025 a large sample of British workers said that the argument about where they work had become stressful, that the arrangement they had was good for them, and that the cost of changing it would land on their own budgets. What it does not establish is what employers should do. Those are different questions, and the article keeps them further apart than its headline does.
paragraphs.chinese: 所以这篇文章立起来的结论是狭窄而有用的：2025 年夏天，一个大样本的英国职员群体表示，关于在哪里工作的争论已经让他们紧张，他们现有的安排对自己有好处，而改变它的代价会落在自己的预算上。它没有立起来的是雇主应当怎么做。这是两个不同的问题，而文章把它们分得比标题更开。

paragraphs.english: Here is an editor-written practice sentence, not a quotation from the original article: Were the price of the commute counted as part of the salary package, the argument over how many days a week a team should sit together would look less like a question of culture and more like a question of pay.
paragraphs.chinese: 下面是一句编辑自拟的练习句，并非原文引用：如果把通勤的代价计入薪酬方案，那么关于一个团队每周应当一起坐几天，这场争论看起来就不那么像文化问题，而更像薪酬问题。

paragraphs.english: As you read, follow three things. First, who is speaking in each paragraph — the reporter, the poll, the statistics agency, or a named executive. Second, the base of every percentage. Third, the verbs of attribution, "said" and "according to" and "told", because a report earns its credibility from them and loses it when they blur. Then ask what the piece would need in order to become an argument rather than a report, and notice how deliberately it stays on the reporting side.
paragraphs.chinese: 阅读时请跟着三条线索走。第一，每一段里说话的是谁——记者、调查、统计机构，还是点名的企业高管。第二，每个百分比的分母。第三，归属动词，“said”“according to”“told”，因为一篇报道的可信度来自它们，也在它们模糊时丢掉可信度。然后问一句：这篇稿子还需要什么，才能从报道变成论证；再留意它多么刻意地留在报道这一侧。

sentenceNotes.sentence: They were not describing an order they had received; they were describing the effect of expecting one.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 由分号连接的两个并列分句：They were not describing an order... 与 they were describing the effect...，两句都以 they 为主语、were describing 为谓语。
sentenceNotes.structure: 否定与肯定对照；第一句的 an order they had received 是省略了关系代词 that/which 的定语从句，修饰 an order；第二句 the effect of expecting one 中 of expecting one 是介词短语作定语，one 代替 an order，避免重复。
sentenceNotes.translation: 他们描述的不是自己已经收到的命令，而是预期会有命令所带来的影响。
sentenceNotes.tip: 分号在这里把“否定什么”和“肯定什么”直接顶在一起，比用 but 更简洁，是英文议论文常见的对照写法。one 是代词，回指前面的 an order：expecting one = expecting an order。读到时先把 one 还原成名词，句子立刻清楚。

sentenceNotes.sentence: The first is a share of all the workers surveyed, the second a share of the hybrid workers inside that group, and news writing compresses such distinctions because space is short.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 三个并列成分由逗号和 and 连接：The first is a share...、the second (is) a share...、news writing compresses such distinctions...；核心是最后一句。
sentenceNotes.structure: the second a share of... 是省略谓语的并列结构（承前省略 is）；surveyed 是过去分词后置修饰 all the workers；inside that group 是介词短语修饰 the hybrid workers；because space is short 是原因状语从句。
sentenceNotes.translation: 前者是全部受访职员中的比例，后者是该群体中混合办公者的比例，而新闻写作因为篇幅紧张会压缩这类区分。
sentenceNotes.tip: 英文常用“承前省略”避免重复动词：the second a share = the second is a share。这类省略在长句里最容易读丢主语，遇到 the second、the latter 一类词，主动补回谓语。distinction 指“区分”，compress such distinctions 意为把本来不同的两类数据混在一句话里。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Were the price of the commute counted as part of the salary package, the argument over how many days a week a team should sit together would look less like a question of culture and more like a question of pay.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 主句为 the argument... would look less like a question of culture and more like a question of pay；从句 Were the price of the commute counted... 是省略 if 的虚拟条件句。
sentenceNotes.structure: Were + 主语 + 过去分词 = If ... were done 的倒装形式，表示与现在事实相反的假设；over how many days a week a team should sit together 是介词短语修饰 the argument，其中 how many days... 是宾语从句；look less like A and more like B 是“看起来不太像 A、更像 B”的对比结构。
sentenceNotes.translation: 如果把通勤的代价计入薪酬方案，那么关于一个团队每周应当一起坐几天，这场争论看起来就不那么像文化问题，而更像薪酬问题。
sentenceNotes.tip: 这句是本站编辑自拟的练习句，不是原文引用，只用于练习结构。虚拟条件句省略 if 后把 were 提前，语气比 if 从句更书面；less like A and more like B 是英语里压缩对比的固定框架，写作时可直接套用。
